Government should treat all people equally regardless of their beliefs.

This principle reflects the importance of lawful and stable governance that respects the social order. In a well-functioning society, equal treatment under the law reinforces trust in institutions and upholds the unity of the collective. Authorities that administer laws and policies uniformly strengthen social cohesion by ensuring that all citizens are subject to the same standards and protections. This approach aligns with maintaining peace, harmony, and the overall stability of the nation, which benefits everyone when applied within the framework of established norms and regulations.

Such a stance does not imply endorsement of ideas that contradict the shared values or security of the community. Rather, it affirms that the government's role is to safeguard the collective well-being by treating individuals equally in matters of rights and duties, provided their conduct remains within the boundaries set by law and social consensus. This reinforces the idea that stability and order depend on consistent, fair application of rules—an essential component of enduring societal trust and progress.
